text.p: Consumer products company Inchcape Timuran Bhd has received the Securities Commission's approval to buy Idris Hydraulic (M) Bhd's entire interest in a finance company for 390 million ringgit.

Inchcape said it also has the Securities Commission's approval for the planned disposal of its entire existing consumer products business in Malaysia. The prosposal was first announced in August 1995.
The Securities Commission's approval clears the way for Inchcape's move out of the consumer products industry, and into financial services.
The purchase of Kewangan Bersatu Bhd (KBB) was to comprise a payment of 94.80 million ringgit in cash and an issue of 80 million new Inchcape shares at 3.69 ringgit each.

However, Inchcape said in a statement that the Securities Commission has revised the issue price of the new shares to 4.40 ringgit per share from the proposed 3.69 ringgit. The number of new Inchcape shares to be issued for the proposed acquisition has been revised to 67.09 million, it said.
The issue price of the new Inchcape shares to be issued pursuant to a proposed one-for-one rights issue was also revised to 3.00 ringgit per share from a proposed 2.40 ringgit.
Inchcape's proposed one-for-four bonus issue and 120 million ringgit bond issue with detachable warrants were also approved.
Inchcape shares closed at 9.30 ringgit on Wednesday.
